text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA

- President Glafcos Clerides issues a stern warning to those who may attempt to cause incidents after the killings of two Greek Cypriots last month in clashes along the Green Line dividing the south of the island from the Turkish-held north.
- Cyprus police crack illegal betting ring.
- United Nations envoy on Cyprus will go to Athens and Ankara after visiting Nicosia next week.
CYPRUS MAIL
- No new taxes as government unveils budget.
- South Australian opposition leader Mike Rann calls for a larger United Nations peacekeeping force in Cyprus.
- Greek Cypriot group calls for more cash for lobbying purposes in the United States.
HARAVGHI
- Conservative party Disy is looking for a successor to President Clerides, believing his re-election in 1998 unlikely because of his inconsistent policies.
- The United Nations and Britain are pushing for a meeting between Clerides and (Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf) Denktash.
- State budgets to be tabled to the House of Representatives for approval on September 19.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Any American initiative on Cyprus should be expected only after elections in the United States in November.
- Government payroll and development projects are widening the deficit.
- Work stoppage planned at Limassol port.
SIMERINI
- Budgets show a deficit of 388.8 million pounds.
- Cabinet rejects Supreme Court judges' request for a pay rise.
- President Clerides hints that telecommunication lines close to the ceasefire line will be moved for security reasons.
